title: LANDFALL BAND
subtitle: Wearable sensing concept: annotated block diagram and reference bill of materials

status.text: Block-level concept. No schematic capture, no PCB, never built, never bench-tested. Every current, rate and size here is a design estimate unless its chip says otherwise.
status.why_no_schematic: KiCad was not available during the hackathon, so the plan's pre-agreed fallback (annotated block diagram plus BOM) is the deliverable.

principle: The band measures what a wearable can measure. Everything else reaches LANDFALL through a documented interface, drawn as NOT MEASURABLE HERE. It is the same discipline as the software: no number without a source, no measurement without a sensor.
label_rule: Every block carries three labels: (a) the indicator it produces, (b) the LANDFALL rule, baseline or case it feeds, and (c) the NASA requirement that justifies or constrains it.

relations.constraint: limits how this block may be built
relations.analogy: written for another system; the band borrows the pattern and does not claim compliance
relations.delegates: assigns this measurement or alert to another system
relations.reference: NASA page that names the measurement (not a requirement)

gap.claim: NASA publishes no minimum sensor set for exploration missions.
gap.detail: The ExMC medical system concept of operations for Mars assumes the crew wears biosensors and defines a Crew Health and Performance Data System, but gives no sensor list, no sampling rates and no specifications. Seven distinct NTRS API queries found nothing that does. The band is one concrete, citable answer to a question NASA has left open.
gap.doc: NASA Exploration Medical Capability. Medical System Concept of Operations for Mars Exploration Mission-11
gap.verified_in: project preparation (PLANO section 1.5); the PDF is not frozen in this build

flown_reference.name: CSA Bio-Monitor (Hexoskin Astroskin)
facts: On the ISS since December 2018; first 48-h session by CSA astronaut David Saint-Jacques (ISS Daily Summary, 2019-02-28).
Validated in HERA Campaign 3, TRL 5 to 6 (NTRS 20190001996).
48 h autonomy on 2 rechargeable AA cells, 400+ h of raw local storage, Bluetooth 2.1, 62 × 78 × 23 mm, 75 g.
Exports EDF, CSV, JSON and binary RIFF/WAV; time base 1/256 s.
flown_reference.basis: Transcribed in the project plan (PLANO section 1.5) from the product's datatype registry. Not re-verified in this build.

channels.resolution: 12 bit, LSB 6.4 µV, 26 mV range, band-pass 1.6-33.9 Hz

anchors.quote: Assessing, recording, monitoring, and trending vital signs and additional physiological and behavioral health signs.
anchors.why: The root requirement for the whole product: in-mission medical capability includes monitoring and trending vital signs.

anchors.quote: Periodic monitoring of general health status.
anchors.why: In-mission preventive care includes periodic monitoring: the band is the periodic, passive part of it.

anchors.quote: Medical equipment shall be usable by non-physician crewmembers in the event that a physician crewmember is not present or is the one who requires medical treatment.
anchors.why: No settings to tune: the band has no screen and no calibration step; the crew wears it, docks it to charge, and LANDFALL does the rest.

anchors.quote: The system shall allow the crewmember to effectively input, store, receive, display, process, distribute, update, monitor and dispose of relevant information on consumable levels, suit status and alerts, and biomedical data.
anchors.why: Written for suits. It is the nearest NASA text on a worn system that handles biomedical data; its rationale asks for real-time heart rhythm and derived core temperature.

anchors.quote: Systems shall automatically record suit pressure, ppO2, and ppCO2. / Suits shall display suit pressure, ppO2, and ppCO2 data to the suited crewmember. / Suits shall monitor suit pressure, ppO2, and ppCO2 and alert the crewmember when they are outside safe limits.
anchors.why: Record, display, alert: the triad NASA requires of a worn system, written for the suit atmosphere, not for biomedical data. The band records; LANDFALL displays and alerts.

anchors.quote: The system shall provide visual indication when a data parameter is stale, missing, unavailable, or unknown.
anchors.why: The band reports off-wrist time and the age of its last sync, so LANDFALL can mark band data STALE or MISSING instead of showing a value that is not current.

buses.label: SPI
buses.detail: SPI, one chip select per AFE

buses.label: I2C-B
buses.detail: I2C bus B: second skin sensor on its own bus, so the two identical parts never contend for one address

buses.label: QSPI
buses.detail: Quad SPI to the log flash

buses.label: BLE 5
buses.detail: Bluetooth LE, encrypted link, to the LANDFALL app on the crew tablet (onboard network; no Earth link needed)

blocks.name: ECG AFE
blocks.function: Single-lead ECG biopotential front end with an on-chip R-to-R interval detector, read over two dry electrodes on the inner face of the band.

source.arithmetic: Bio-Monitor ECG 256 Hz, kept at 256 sps
Bio-Monitor HRV over 300 s, kept at 300 s (5-min windows)

produces.label: Resting heart rate
produces.how: lowest stable 5-min heart rate in the main sleep period, from R-R intervals

produces.label: Heart rate variability (SDNN)
produces.how: SDNN of normal-to-normal intervals over 5-min windows in sleep

justified_by.quote: Assessing, recording, monitoring, and trending vital signs and additional physiological and behavioral health signs.
Derived body core temperature and heart rhythm (real-time) are desired for microgravity operations
justified_by.note: From the rationale; written for suits.

justified_by.quote: For equipment such as bioinstrumentation and medical devices, that are specifically designed to contact the human body, electrical leakage currents caused by contact with exposed surfaces (including in worst-case fault scenarios) shall be kept below the levels specified in Table 9.3-11

limits.what: Leakage, external contact, DC to 1 kHz, normal
Leakage, external contact, DC to 1 kHz, single fault

design: R-R intervals, not waveforms, are logged: the whole flash would hold only about 6 h of raw ECG (see the log arithmetic).
The band does not estimate blood pressure from ECG-to-PPG transit time (see the Bio-Monitor pitfalls).

blocks.name: PPG / SpO2 AFE
blocks.function: Optical front end: drives red and infrared LEDs and reads the photodiode for pulse and SpO2 spot windows.
mfr_spec: LED drivers and photodiode readout on chip

source.arithmetic: Bio-Monitor PPG 64 Hz, kept at 64 Hz
Bio-Monitor SpO2 1 Hz, kept at 1 Hz

source.rationale: LED current dominates the power budget; ECG already gives heart rate, so the optical channel runs in windows (10 % duty).

produces.label: SpO2 (spot windows)
produces.how: recorded and shown as context; no LANDFALL rule uses it

produces.label: Pulse rate (backup)
produces.how: backup source for resting heart rate when ECG electrode contact is lost

feeds.as: NASA publishes no in-flight SpO2 limit, and LANDFALL does not invent one

justified_by.quote: Assessing, recording, monitoring, and trending vital signs and additional physiological and behavioral health signs.
Any surface to which the bare skin of the crew is exposed shall not cause skin temperature to enter the range for pain/injury in Table 9.3-5

limits.rationale: 2 °C below the start of the Table 9.3-5 pain range; read from the skin temperature sensors.

design: Each sample is timestamped at acquisition on the MCU clock and the AFE's fixed pipeline delay is written in the log header, never assumed to be zero (see the Nonin 172 ms pitfall).

blocks.name: Spectral light sensor
blocks.function: 11-channel spectral sensor on the outer face: synthesises photopic lux plus red, green and blue bands for daytime light exposure.
mfr_spec: 11 channels: 8 visible bands, clear, near-IR, flicker

source.rationale: One reading per 1-min epoch, the epoch length of research wrist actigraphs (Actiwatch Spectrum, per the project plan).

produces.label: Daytime light exposure (wrist)
produces.how: mean photopic illuminance at the wrist during the scheduled wake period

feeds.as: ground packet; closes the loop from sensor to the lighting countermeasure

justified_by.quote: measurements of activity and light exposure (gathered through a wrist sensor)
The system shall provide the levels of light to support the physiological effects of light in accordance with Table 8.7-2
justified_by.note: Table 8.7-2 is specified as melanopic EDI at the cornea, for the lighting system. A wrist reading is not that quantity, so it is context and never a compliance check.

limits.what: General ambient, melanopic EDI at cornea
Crew pre-sleep, melanopic EDI at cornea

design: Nobody else puts a spectral sensor on a crew wearable; it is the band's most defensible part, because the circadian countermeasure is a lighting prescription.

blocks.name: Skin temperature, 2 sites
blocks.function: Two digital skin-temperature sensors on the inner face. They also act as the skin-side safety monitor for the LEDs and the cell.

source.arithmetic: Bio-Monitor skin temperature, 2 channels at 1 Hz, kept at 2 × 1 Hz

produces.label: Skin temperature
produces.how: median skin temperature in the main sleep period

justified_by.quote: Assessing, recording, monitoring, and trending vital signs and additional physiological and behavioral health signs.
Any surface to which the bare skin of the crew is exposed shall not cause skin temperature to exceed the injury limits in Table 9.3-4

design: Skin temperature is not core temperature. The band does not derive core temperature: that needs a validated model, which is an open item.
Skin temperature follows cabin temperature and clothing, so LANDFALL shows it as context and never alerts on it.

blocks.name: IMU (actigraphy)
blocks.function: 6-axis IMU. Only the accelerometer runs, for actigraphy (sleep and wake scoring) and off-wrist detection.

source.rationale: Between the 32 Hz of research wrist actigraphs (per the project plan) and the 64 Hz of the flown Bio-Monitor accelerometer; 52 Hz is a native output rate of the part.
1-min epochs, as in research actigraphy; the same epoch as the light sensor.

produces.label: Sleep duration (actigraphy)
produces.how: total sleep time in the main sleep period, scored from 1-min activity epochs

produces.label: Sleep midpoint shift
produces.how: shift of the night's sleep midpoint from the baseline median

justified_by.quote: measurements of activity and light exposure (gathered through a wrist sensor)
Assessing, recording, monitoring, and trending vital signs and additional physiological and behavioral health signs.

design: Actigraphy is how Barger et al. (Lancet Neurol 2014) measured astronaut sleep in flight: 6.09 h per night on the ISS.
Off-wrist time (no motion and skin temperature near cabin temperature) is logged as MISSING, never as zero activity or as sleep.

blocks.name: MCU + BLE radio
blocks.function: Reads every sensor, timestamps every sample on one clock, writes the local log and syncs it to the LANDFALL app over an encrypted BLE link when the tablet is in range.
mfr_spec: QSPI, SPI and two I2C controllers
blocks.produces_note: No indicator of its own. It turns raw samples into timestamped epoch records; the LANDFALL app computes the nightly indicators, so one engine evaluates every source the same way.

justified_by.quote: The system shall have features for the protection of sensitive and private data, transmission, secure viewing, and sender verification.
justified_by.note: Encrypted, bonded BLE link; the band stores no names, only a crew id.

justified_by.quote: The system shall provide alternative information sources for use in the event of the loss of the information management system.
justified_by.note: If the tablet fails, the band keeps recording on its own.

design: One real-time clock stamps every channel in mission elapsed time (MET), so channels align without guessing delays.

blocks.name: Local log, 16 MiB
blocks.function: 128 Mbit serial NOR flash: the band's own log. The no-comms thesis applied to the device itself: nothing is lost when the tablet is out of range or down.
blocks.produces_note: Stores, does not measure. Depth arithmetic below.

feeds.as: keeps one whole 14-day RCI baseline window on the band

justified_by.quote: The system shall provide for 1) automatic backup and crew restoration of information essential for system functionality, and 2) crew-initiated backup and restoration of information that can be generated or changed by crew during the mission.
The system shall provide environmental and suit monitoring data in formats compatible with performing temporal trend analyses.
justified_by.note: Written for environmental and suit data. The band's records are timestamped and trend-ready, and export as FHIR R4 Observations through LANDFALL.

design: NASA publishes no requirement for wearable storage or log duration, so the 14-day target is a design choice.

blocks.name: LiPo cell 200 mAh
blocks.function: Single lithium-polymer cell, 3.7 V nominal, sized to sit far inside the JSC-20793 Non-Critical battery class.

justified_by.doc: JSC-20793 Rev D, Crewed Space Vehicle Battery Safety Requirements
justified_by.quote: Non-Critical: less than 4 Wh per isolated pack; Li-ion COTS cells up to 1000 mAh.
justified_by.note: Class boundaries as read in project preparation (PLANO Appendix B); the document is not frozen in this build.

limits.what: Non-Critical class, energy per isolated pack

blocks.name: Charger
blocks.function: Single-cell linear Li-ion/LiPo charge controller, fed from the 5 V charging dock.

justified_by.doc: JSC-20793 Rev D, Crewed Space Vehicle Battery Safety Requirements
justified_by.quote: Section 4.4.3 asks for monitoring of battery voltage, current and temperature.
justified_by.note: This part has no thermistor input, so charging is not temperature-qualified: an open item.

blocks.name: Fuel gauge
blocks.function: Cell voltage and state of charge over I2C, so LANDFALL can show band battery and warn before the band stops recording.
mfr_spec: ModelGauge state of charge from cell voltage, no sense resistor

justified_by.doc: JSC-20793 Rev D, Crewed Space Vehicle Battery Safety Requirements
justified_by.quote: Section 4.4.3 asks for monitoring of battery voltage, current and temperature.
justified_by.note: This gauge measures voltage only; it measures neither current nor temperature. Closing 4.4.3 needs a coulomb-counting gauge with a thermistor input: an open item.

power.summary: Average-current budget and autonomy. Every current is an estimate from typical datasheet figures, never measured on a bench, so the budget carries a 2× margin.

budget.label: nRF52840: CPU duty, BLE sync, clock

budget_source.rationale: Typical datasheet figures for these duty cycles; to be replaced by bench measurement.

steps.label: Margin for unmeasured currents
steps.rationale: Nothing here has been measured; doubling is our hedge.

steps.label: Cell capacity
steps.rationale: Small enough for a band, five times under the 1000 mAh Non-Critical cell limit.

steps.label: Cell energy
steps.arithmetic: 3.7 V × 0.200 Ah = 0.74 Wh, 5.4 times below the 4 Wh Non-Critical limit

steps.label: Autonomy target
steps.rationale: One whole case tripwire window on one charge: cases.json reassess_after_s = 259,200 s (72 h) for renal_stone and sleep_circadian.

power.comparison: The flown Bio-Monitor runs 48 h on 2 AA cells, but it records 3-lead ECG at 256 Hz, respiration at 128 Hz and continuous PPG. The band records fewer, slower channels on purpose.
power.no_requirement: NASA publishes no battery-endurance requirement for wearables: all three mentions of battery in Vol 2 Rev F are about other things. The 72 h target is ours.

log.summary: What 16 MiB holds. NASA publishes no storage or log-duration requirement for wearables, so every target here is a design choice.

steps.label: Reserved: raw ECG event ring
steps.rationale: 4 MiB of raw ECG around flagged events, for the flight surgeon.

steps.label: R-R intervals at 100 bpm, 2 B each
steps.arithmetic: 100 beats/min × 1,440 min × 2 B = 288,000 B/day (100 bpm is a deliberately high planning rate: design choice)

steps.label: 1-min epoch records, 32 B each
steps.arithmetic: 1,440 epochs × 32 B = 46,080 B/day (activity, light bands, 2 skin temperatures, SpO2 window, flags, MET: design choice)

steps.label: Log depth target
steps.rationale: One whole RCI baseline window: personal.json rci.baseline_window_days = 14. A lost tablet does not cost anyone their baseline.

steps.label: Raw ECG rate
steps.arithmetic: 256 samples/s × 3 B (18-bit sample in 3 bytes) = 768 B/s

steps.label: Raw ECG in the event ring
Raw ECG if the whole flash held it
steps.arithmetic: 16,777,216 B / 768 B/s = 21,845 s = 6.1 h. This is why the band logs R-R intervals, not waveforms.

not_measurable_here.what: Urine output and fluid intake (24 h)
not_measurable_here.why: No wearable measures urine volume or what a crewmember drinks.

Alerting on exposure rates is assigned to the vehicle's radiation monitoring system, and organ dose in mGy-Eq needs that system's detectors and models. LANDFALL does not duplicate it with a wrist sensor.

requirement.quote: The radiation monitoring system shall alert the crew and operations teams when radiation exposure rates exceed predefined thresholds.

examples.name: ISS TEPC (NASA SRAG, JSC)
examples.text: tissue-equivalent proportional counter; measured ISS dose rate, frozen in this build

examples.name: CSA CANS
examples.text: "a compact and autonomous instrument designed to measure neutron radiation exposure in space"; neutrons are about 30 % of ISS radiation (CSA)

not_measurable_here.why: Needs a blood draw or a urine sample and an analyser.
not_measurable_here.via: Laboratory: ground analysis of returned samples

examples.name: OSDR Inspiration4 panels
examples.text: real per-subject reference ranges, measured before and after flight only

not_measurable_here.why: Wrist transit-time methods give systolic only and need per-subject calibration (see the Bio-Monitor pitfalls).

examples.name: Tempus Pro (NASA HRP)
examples.text: NASA tested this telemedicine device; it collects "blood pressure, heart rate, respiration rate, and temperature". NASA's article does not say how its blood pressure is measured.

feeds.as: NASA publishes no in-flight blood pressure limit

not_measurable_here.why: Needs a graded exercise test, with gas exchange or a validated indirect protocol.

requirement.quote: Crewmembers shall maintain an in-mission VO2max at or above 36.5 ml⁄min/kg for missions with extraterrestrial surface EVAs as determined by either direct or indirect measures.

not_measurable_here.via: Ground DXA before and after flight

requirement.quote: Countermeasures shall maintain bone mineral density of the hip and spine at or above 95% of pre-mission values and at or above 90% for the femoral neck.

not_measurable_here.why: An atmosphere measurement, not a body one.

requirement.quote: The system shall alert the crew locally and remotely when atmospheric parameters, including atmospheric pressure, humidity, temperature, ppO2, and ppCO2 are outside safe limits.

not_measurable_here.what: Circadian phase and light at the eye
not_measurable_here.why: Phase needs melatonin or core temperature; Table 8.7-2 specifies light at the cornea, not at the wrist.
not_measurable_here.via: Research protocol; vehicle lighting system or a corneal light meter

requirement.quote: The system shall provide the levels of light to support the physiological effects of light in accordance with Table 8.7-2

negatives.claim: No EMI/EMC requirement exists in NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Rev F.
negatives.detail: The only electromagnetic requirement is human RF exposure, [V2 6102]. Citing a [V2] number for EMC would be fabrication; EMC qualification comes from the program.
Nearest: [V2 7076] clothing comfort and composition, and [V2 7081] microbiologically safe surfaces; material assessment is deferred to NASA-STD-6016.

negatives.claim: NASA publishes no minimum sensor set for exploration missions.
negatives.detail: No wearable, biosensor or body-worn device requirement in Vol 2 Rev F; the ExMC Mars medical ConOps (NTRS 20200001715) assumes "All crewmembers are wearing biosensors" with no sensor list, rates or specifications.
Vol 2 Rev F mentions batteries 3 times, about traverse power projection and maintenance, never endurance. The autonomy target is a design choice.

negatives.claim: No data storage or log-duration requirement.
negatives.detail: Zero hits for storage capacity, retention or log duration. The log-depth target is a design choice.
negatives.pattern: data storage|storage capacity|data retention|retention period|log duration|logging duration

pitfalls.title: Its blood pressure is systolic-only and PTT-derived
pitfalls.text: The Bio-Monitor's blood pressure is not a cuff reading and not continuous: it is systolic only, derived from pulse transit time between the ECG QRS and the PPG, and the useful form is adjusted to the user, so it needs per-subject calibration.
pitfalls.consequence: The band does not estimate blood pressure. Blood pressure is a hand-off to the cuff in the medical kit.

pitfalls.title: The Nonin sensor adds a 172 ms delay
pitfalls.text: The digital output of the Bio-Monitor's Nonin sensor lags by 172 ms, which must be subtracted when computing pulse transit time.
pitfalls.consequence: Every band channel is timestamped at acquisition on one clock, and each front end's fixed delay is written in the log header.

pitfalls.title: CSV and JSON exports cap at 65,536 values per datatype
pitfalls.text: About 18 h at 1 Hz, so high-rate channels require the binary path.
pitfalls.consequence: R-R intervals at 100 bpm reach 65,536 values in 10.9 h, so they leave the band in binary records; 1-min epochs would take 45.5 days to reach the cap.

pitfalls_basis: Verified in project preparation against the product documentation (PLANO section 1.5). Not frozen in this build.

safety.text: External contact, DC to 1 kHz: 0.1 mA normal, 0.5 mA single fault. The electrodes are the band's only conductive skin contact.

safety.topic: Current through the crewmember, any equipment
safety.text: Nominal: 0.4 mA DC, 0.2 mA peak AC. Startle: 2 mA DC, 0.5 mA AC. Catastrophic: 40 mA DC, 8 mA peak AC.
The crew must be able to interrupt power and see the de-energized status. The band has no switch or status light in this BOM: an open item.
Tissue damage at 49 °C or above (Table 9.3-4); pain range 43 to 49 °C (Table 9.3-5). The LEDs stop at 41 °C at the skin-side sensor (design choice).
The BLE radio must keep crew RF exposure within Table 6.8-2. This is the only electromagnetic requirement in Vol 2.

Non-Critical: under 4 Wh per isolated pack, Li-ion COTS up to 1000 mAh. Critical: 1-fault tolerant, under 20 V and 60 Wh. Catastrophic: 2-fault tolerant. Section 4.4.3: monitor voltage, current and temperature.

Test 1 flammability (5 specimens of 30 × 6.5 cm, none burns more than 15 cm), Test 4 wire insulation, Test 7 offgassing (72 ± 1 h at 50 ± 3 °C, total T value under 0.5), Test 18 arc tracking. An untested material needs a Material Usage Agreement under NASA-STD-6016C.

safety_basis: Vol 2 Rev F items are frozen in std_vol2_requirements. JSC-20793 and NASA-STD-6001B were read in project preparation (PLANO Appendix B) and are not frozen in this build.
open_items: No schematic capture or PCB: block level only (KiCad not available).
Every current in the power budget is a datasheet-typical estimate; bench measurement replaces it.

Battery monitoring: the MCP73831 has no thermistor input and the MAX17048 measures neither current nor temperature, so JSC-20793 section 4.4.3 is not met yet. Fix: a coulomb-counting gauge with a thermistor input.
No power switch or status light for [V2 9017] / [V2 9018].
Power tree (1.8 V AFE rail, LED supply) not designed.
Electrode material, strap and housing materials not selected: NASA-STD-6001B testing or a Material Usage Agreement is needed.
Core body temperature is not derived: that needs a validated model.
Check the MAX30208 addressing on the datasheet before layout; the two-bus split avoids the question for now.
